domain_assessment.domain: Manufacturing production planning and control in a metal-stamping operation
domain_assessment.role: PPC analyst responsible for a rolling five-day schedule across Presses 1, 2, and 3 and coordination with three downstream assembly plants
domain_assessment.objective: Maintain production continuity and on-time downstream shipments while responding to a demand surge, supplier-delay risk, and escalating equipment-reliability risk
domain_assessment.incident_type: Multi-source operational disruption involving incremental demand, coil-steel supplier delay, and a vibration-related reliability concern on the only currently tooled press for a required part

decision_points.summary: Monday capacity-allocation decision: allocate the full incremental bracket batch to Press 3 rather than split work with a temporarily retooled Press 1 or defer volume.
evidence_before: Weekend demand surge from a downstream assembly plant
Requirement for an extra batch of a high-volume bracket variant
Press 3 was the only press currently tooled for that variant
Prior-week throughput report showed Press 3 ran above target
A brief scheduling-assistant flag indicated that Press 3 had an open low-priority vibration advisory
The full CMMS advisory detail was available only through further lookup
evidence_after: Maintenance technician later described a recommended follow-up inspection within two weeks
Participant said a dashboard-integrated advisory would have caused a longer pause before allocation
goals_constraints: Avoid Press 1 retooling and partial-changeover cost
Use the only currently tooled press
alternatives: Allocate the full incremental batch to Press 3
Split the batch between a reduced Press 3 run and a temporarily retooled Press 1
Push part of the order into the following week
decision_points.decision_basis: Recent throughput evidence was explicitly treated as more informative and decision-relevant than the abbreviated low-priority vibration flag.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate to high due to the demand surge and schedule implications, but not so extreme that consideration of the known flag was impossible.
decision_points.uncertainty: Whether prior-week throughput adequately represented safe incremental loading given an existing, though abbreviated, vibration-related maintenance advisory.

decision_points.summary: Tuesday supplier-response decision: interpret the current four-day coil-steel delay as part of an apparently recurring timing pattern and use one familiar backup supplier contact without comparing available alternatives.
evidence_before: Supplier representative announced a four-day delay
Supplier representative cited "internal allocation constraints"
Participant recalled two previous supplier delays, around late December and late June
Both previous delays resolved within a week without requiring backup stock
Participant had an established relationship with one backup supplier
evidence_after: Participant contacted the familiar supplier as a reserve
Participant did not compare lead times or pricing across alternate suppliers
Participant did not order backup stock immediately
goals_constraints: Protect production against a raw-material supply interruption
Respond amid concurrent production and reliability issues
Use limited time and attention efficiently
alternatives: Contact the known backup supplier as a reserve
Compare multiple backup suppliers on lead time, price, and availability
Wait for the primary supplier delay to resolve
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant treated apparent timing regularity in earlier supplier delays as more diagnostic than the representative's current allocation-constraint explanation and selected the first familiar acceptable fallback source under time pressure.
decision_points.time_pressure: High; the participant states that there was no clean window for comparative supplier evaluation while other matters were active.
decision_points.uncertainty: Whether the current allocation-constraint delay had the same causal mechanism, expected duration, and supply-risk implications as the previous delays.

decision_points.summary: Thursday information-seeking decision: defer review of an available three-week vibration trend log after learning that Press 3 vibration had increased slightly.
evidence_before: Reliability engineer reported that Press 3 vibration had ticked up slightly since the weekend run
A full three-week vibration trend log was available
The participant had a vivid memory of a previous Press 1 fire
A bi-weekly maintenance review was approaching
evidence_after: Participant did not review the full trend log
Participant acknowledged that the log might have shown a clearer upward trend
Participant acknowledged that a clearer trend could have required reworking Friday's plan
Engineering raised Press 3 status to "elevated concern" on Friday
goals_constraints: Determine whether the reliability signal required immediate scheduling intervention
Avoid unnecessary disruption to the production schedule
Manage workload during a fast-moving week
Preserve the option to address the issue in the upcoming maintenance review
alternatives: Review the full trend log immediately
Ask reliability engineering for additional interpretation
Defer detailed review to the bi-weekly maintenance meeting
Treat the single update as insufficiently urgent to justify further investigation
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant characterized the single update as non-dramatic, judged seriousness against a vivid past failure, and deferred access to information that might have compelled difficult rescheduling.
decision_points.time_pressure: Present and meaningful, though not absolute; the participant had access to the trend log and consciously elected not to inspect it.
decision_points.uncertainty: Whether the modest reported increase was isolated variation or evidence of an unfavorable and operationally significant trend.

decision_points.summary: Friday schedule-commitment decision: retain most of the confirmed Press 3 plan after engineering upgraded the status to "elevated concern," while making only a limited reduction in Friday loading.
evidence_before: Engineering upgraded Press 3 from "monitor" to "elevated concern"
The engineer clarified that the change reflected a real increase in loading risk
Downstream plants had already received schedule confirmation
Reallocation to Press 1 would require several hours of partial changeover
Participant retained confidence in prior throughput data and the clean weekend run
evidence_after: Participant trimmed Friday's Press 3 run slightly
Participant did not substantially reallocate or overhaul the schedule
Press 3 completed the week without failure
Reliability filed a formal recommendation to reduce loading in the next cycle
goals_constraints: Respond proportionately to new reliability information
alternatives: Delay part of the required production volume
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant explicitly gave earlier throughput and weekend-run evidence more weight than the newly clarified elevated-concern signal.
decision_points.time_pressure: High because the schedule was being finalized and downstream plants had already received confirmation.
decision_points.uncertainty: The interview does not quantify failure probability or downtime timing, but the new engineering information clearly indicates an increase in loading risk.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “The flag was there, but it was low-priority and vague next to a full week of solid output numbers, so the throughput report just carried more weight for me.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Monday allocation follow-up after the interviewer asks why throughput was decisive despite the vibration flag.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant possessed both confirming throughput evidence and potentially disconfirming advisory information before allocating the full batch. The participant explicitly assigned greater weight to the evidence supporting Press 3 capacity and discounted the advisory as insufficient to change the preferred allocation.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The throughput report was detailed, recent, and directly relevant to production capacity, whereas the advisory flag was abbreviated, vague, and low priority. A scheduler could reasonably assign the report more weight absent clearer reliability-risk information.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. The interview identifies the two evidence sources, the allocation decision, and the participant's relative weighting of those sources.

revision.location: Decision point 1, Monday allocation chronology and the follow-up on why throughput was decisive.
revision.current_defect: None material. The participant now has pre-decision awareness of the advisory and explicitly describes selective relative weighting.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: No revision required. Retain the abbreviated advisory flag, the throughput report, and the participant's explanation that the report carried more weight.
preserve: The availability of fuller CMMS detail through separate lookup
The participant's selection of full Press 3 allocation
avoid_creating: A second information-avoidance episode at decision point 1
An additional conservatism episode before the Friday escalation

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I didn't compare lead times or pricing against other options that morning — there wasn't a clean window to do that kind of comparison shopping with everything else going on.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Tuesday follow-up concerning the choice of backup supplier contact.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant selected the first familiar and acceptable backup-supplier option under time and attention constraints instead of conducting comparative search and evaluation of sourcing alternatives. This is distinct from the participant's causal inference about why the primary supplier's delay would resolve.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Contacting a known qualified supplier first can be an efficient and appropriate operational response when the purpose is only to create a reserve option and time is limited.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. The text establishes an alternative-selection process, a constrained search, a familiar fallback, and the absence of comparative evaluation.

revision.current_defect: None material. The satisficing mechanism is independently identifiable.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: No revision required. Retain the participant's familiar supplier relationship, time constraint, and lack of comparison across other suppliers.
preserve: The supplier was contacted as a reserve
The distinction from causal interpretation of the primary supplier delay
avoid_creating: A second alternative-selection episode involving stock quantity
An assertion that the known supplier was objectively poor or unavailable
A merged causal-attribution and supplier-choice explanation

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “Their delays always seem to cluster around certain stretches for them, so I read the timing itself as the real signal — the ‘internal allocation constraints’ line sounded like their usual wording, not something new.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Tuesday supplier-delay chronology and the later reasoning probe about waiting rather than ordering backup stock.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant treats a superficial timing pattern drawn from two earlier supplier delays as the causal explanatory signal for the current event and discounts the supplier's current allocation-based explanation as routine wording. The inference goes beyond using history as a forecast; it assigns causal significance to temporal co-occurrence without establishing a shared mechanism.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Historical supplier performance may be relevant if the participant has reliable operational knowledge that this supplier repeatedly experiences seasonal or cyclical allocation stress. The interview, however, provides only two broad temporal reference points and no evidence of a verified common cause.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None for the hidden specification's requested causal-misattribution mechanism. The participant now explicitly identifies timing as the perceived real signal and dismisses a potentially competing current explanation.

revision.current_defect: None material. The interview now contains causal temporal-pattern reasoning rather than merely a past-case similarity forecast.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: No revision required. Retain the participant's statement that timing was treated as more informative than the current allocation-constraint explanation.
avoid_creating: An explicit claim that timing proves causation
A causal explanation based solely on supplier distrust or relationship history

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “Even with the engineer telling me it reflected a real risk increase, the earlier data — the throughput numbers, the clean weekend run — still felt like the more solid read on how Press 3 actually performs, so I didn't weight the new label as heavily as what I already had.”
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant receives clarified new engineering evidence of increased loading risk, but explicitly weights it less heavily than the prior throughput-based assessment and clean-weekend belief. The participant makes a modest adjustment but preserves most of the original plan, demonstrating insufficient belief updating relative to the stated new information.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The schedule was already confirmed downstream, Press 1 changeover would consume several hours, and the interview does not quantify the increased downtime probability. Partial retention of the plan could therefore be operationally defensible.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. The participant's own statement establishes the comparative weighting of prior and new evidence, allowing the mechanism to be distinguished from schedule constraints alone.

revision.location: Decision point 4, Friday explanation of the retained schedule.
revision.current_defect: None material. The new reliability evidence, prior belief, and underweighting relationship are all directly observable.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: No revision required. Retain the engineer's clarification, the participant's relative-weighting statement, the constrained schedule context, and the limited run trim.
preserve: Clarification that elevated concern represented a real loading-risk increase
The distinction from Monday allocation-stage evidence weighting
avoid_creating: A pure sunk-cost or status-quo account that replaces belief updating
An unrealistic refusal to comply with mandatory engineering direction
A duplicate confirmation-bias episode with identical evidence sources

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I was thinking of the Press 1 fire from a couple years ago — that's the reference point that comes to mind when someone says ‘press failure.’ This didn't look anything like that, so it didn't register as urgent.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Thursday probe asking which situation the participant pictured when assessing seriousness.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant assesses the seriousness of a gradual vibration signal by reference to an easily recalled, vivid, catastrophic press-fire incident. Because the current signal lacks the vivid features of that remembered event, it is experienced as lower urgency despite the availability of actual trend data.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A prior serious incident can be a meaningful professional reference case. Here, the participant explicitly identifies that vivid reference as the reason the current gradual indicator did not register as urgent, supporting an imaginability-based mechanism.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. The recalled event, its cognitive salience, and its effect on the participant's urgency assessment are explicit.

revision.location: Decision point 3, recalled-incident probe and answer.
revision.current_defect: None material. The memory-based risk-judgment mechanism is independently observable.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: No revision required. Retain the vivid Press 1 fire reference and the contrast between that dramatic incident and the current gradual vibration issue.
preserve: The participant's statement that this was the reference point that came to mind
The lower urgency assigned to the current vibration signal
avoid_creating: A second vivid-memory mechanism at another decision point
A claim that only catastrophic events warrant reliability action

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “Pulling three weeks of data might have shown a clearer upward line than a single number did, and that could have meant reworking Friday's plan on top of everything else already moving.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Thursday trend-log question and participant response.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant recognizes that available risk-relevant information could reveal an adverse trend and trigger an inconvenient schedule revision, then consciously elects not to inspect that information at the time. The avoidance concerns exposure to potentially decision-forcing evidence, not merely lack of access or an inability to obtain the log.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Deferral to a nearby bi-weekly maintenance review can be legitimate triage if the reported increase is slight, production is under pressure, and no mandatory escalation threshold has yet been met.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. The interview establishes availability of the information, anticipation of the potentially adverse implication, and a conscious decision to defer review.

revision.current_defect: None material. The information-avoidance mechanism is distinct from the vivid-memory risk-judgment mechanism.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: No revision required. Retain the acknowledgement that the log could reveal a clearer worsening trend and could require reworking Friday's plan.
preserve: The possible operational consequence of discovering a worsening trend
avoid_creating: A duplicate conservatism-bias episode at Thursday
An explicit statement that the participant knowingly violated a required reliability process
A participant self-labeling the behavior as avoidance

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “That's the reference point that comes to mind when someone says ‘press failure.’”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The Press 1 fire is readily retrieved and becomes the dominant comparison case in assessing current risk.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This substantially overlaps with the planned Imaginability Bias occurrence and should not be separately counted unless the benchmark taxonomy formally distinguishes availability from imaginability.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “At that point we were locked in with the downstream plants, and a full reallocation meant hours of changeover we didn't have room for.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The established schedule may acquire additional behavioral weight because changing it is disruptive and costly.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The schedule was genuinely committed to downstream plants and reallocation had known material changeover costs. These operational facts are sufficient to explain retention of most of the plan without invoking a preference for the status quo.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “The earlier data — the throughput numbers, the clean weekend run — still felt like the more solid read on how Press 3 actually performs.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: Earlier favorable evidence serves as a reference point from which the participant insufficiently adjusts after receiving newer engineering risk information.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This is conceptually overlapping with the requested Conservatism Bias occurrence rather than a separate accidental manifestation.

nonbias_cues.cue: Press 3 completed the week without failing, and shipments went out on time.
nonbias_cues.location: Outcome question near the end of the interview.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A favorable outcome does not establish that the earlier decision process was unbiased, just as an unfavorable outcome would not itself establish bias. Classification depends on decision-time cognition and information treatment.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant selected a known backup supplier rapidly.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Using a familiar supplier and acting quickly can be rational in a disruption. The bounded-rationality occurrence is supported by the participant's explicit constrained search and absence of comparative evaluation, not by speed alone.

nonbias_cues.cue: The vibration advisory flag was low priority and vague.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Low-priority vague information may reasonably receive less weight than detailed throughput evidence. The confirmation-bias annotation rests on the documented selective evidence weighting, not on an assumption that the advisory should have dictated the decision.

nonbias_cues.cue: Downstream plants had already been confirmed and Press 1 changeover would consume several hours.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: These are genuine organizational and operational constraints. They do not alone demonstrate conservatism bias; the relevant evidence is the participant's explicit underweighting of clarified new engineering information.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant deferred detailed trend review until an upcoming maintenance review.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Deferral can be ordinary prioritization. The Ostrich-effect interpretation is supported only because the participant connects non-review with the possibility that the information would compel immediate schedule rework.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant drew on prior supplier disruptions.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Past supplier experience is potentially valid evidence. It becomes a bias-relevant episode here because the participant treats a thin temporal pattern as the causal signal and dismisses the current explanation without supporting causal evidence.

causal_claims.claim: The timing pattern of earlier supplier delays is treated as the operative cause or most diagnostic explanation of the current supplier delay.
causal_claims.assessment: The transcript supports that the participant made this attribution. The substantive causal inference is weak because two broad time points do not establish a recurring causal mechanism, and the current supplier cites internal allocation constraints.

causal_claims.claim: A full vibration trend log might reveal a clearer upward trajectory and require reworking the Friday production plan.
causal_claims.assessment: This is a plausible participant-level conditional causal expectation. The interview does not quantify the reliability threshold or predicted downtime, but it adequately identifies why the participant viewed the information as potentially decision-forcing.

causal_claims.claim: The Friday elevated-concern status reflected a real increase in loading risk.
causal_claims.assessment: The interview attributes this claim to engineering clarification. It supports the cognitive comparison between new evidence and prior belief, but does not by itself quantify the probability, magnitude, or timing of failure.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The participant infers causal significance from the apparent clustering of two previous supplier delays around broad recurring time periods.
correlation_causation_risks.implication: This is the requested correlation-bias mechanism. The interview appropriately presents it as the participant's reasoning, not as a validated factual explanation of supplier operations.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The fact that Press 3 ultimately did not fail may be read retrospectively as proof that the participant's earlier reliability judgments were correct.
correlation_causation_risks.implication: The successful outcome must remain analytically separate from the quality of the earlier evidence weighting, information-seeking, and belief-updating processes.

causal_audit.changed_variable: Visibility and workflow placement of the existing Monday vibration-advisory flag: separate message from the scheduling assistant versus direct appearance inside the scheduling dashboard beside throughput information.
held_constant: Weekend demand surge and required batch size
Press 3 tooling exclusivity for the bracket variant
Supplier delay timing and stated cause
The production alternatives and their changeover implications
causal_audit.explanation: The counterfactual now isolates the intended workflow-visibility variable. The original condition supplies an abbreviated advisory through a separate scheduling-assistant message, while the changed condition places that same flag directly beside the throughput report in the scheduling dashboard. The participant predicts a longer pause and less reliance on throughput under the changed presentation. Unlike the prior version, the counterfactual does not add advisory detail or change severity, reliability policy, tooling, demand, or schedule constraints. The hidden specification's phrase "logged only in CMMS" is not a material contradiction if interpreted as meaning the underlying detailed advisory remained in CMMS while a brief notification was separately relayed; however, the specification should clarify that distinction if exact treatment fidelity is required.

global_revision_constraints: Preserve the four-decision-point structure: Monday allocation, Tuesday supplier response, Thursday trend-log decision, and Friday schedule commitment.
Do not use the favorable operational outcome to validate or invalidate any cognitive-bias occurrence.
Keep decision point 2 divided into a timing-based causal-attribution episode and a distinct constrained alternative-selection episode.
Keep decision point 3 divided into a vivid-memory-based risk-judgment episode and a distinct information-avoidance episode.
Retain the abbreviated pre-decision advisory flag at decision point 1 so that selective relative weighting remains observable.
Maintain the counterfactual as a single workflow-visibility manipulation without adding advisory detail, changing risk severity, or altering operational constraints.
